messages.subject: cloglog problems for binary data
parts:
Hi,

We've run into some issues with using a cloglog model for binary data (reproducibile in a simple glm).   In particular, we're getting a message of (e.g.) "GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=789" for each observation (and seemingly for each/many iterations).  The problem is not produced when using a logit link or when using the glm() function from base R.

The model does contain an offset, which has large values, but reducing/removing this doesn't seem to have any effect.

I don't know how to fix this problem.  I reckon (uneducated guesses really) that

1) It is a user error
2) There is numerical overflow issues (so that predictions are very slightly above (below) 1 (0))
3) The starting values are very far from the max
4) some combination of 3 and 4.

I have put code and simulated data in a dropbox folder.  Let me know if you can't access it. https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/00e4dko767yn42gnv1zoz/cloglogIssue1.R?rlkey=lr5gbo3488b7kyqt6z662yw2z&dl=0.  Script is pasted below (but data still on dropbox).

Any help is appreciated. Thanks,

Scott


library( INLA)

#data available from https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/tihsg9da53c6ar5z50vet/datPA.RDS?rlkey=im06zt0jnlssz1izpexsne346&dl=0

datPA <- readRDS( "~/play/cloglogIssues/datPA.RDS")

############
#Fit some models using glm()
fmGLM <- list()
#Fit the model that simulated the data. Note offset and pretty small intercept (negative on link scale)
#The fit 'works', up to some possible quasi-separation issues (haven't investigated)
fmGLM$cloglog <- glm( PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset=log(transectArea), data=datPA, family=binomial(link="cloglog"))
#estimates are quite similar to those used to simulate (1.25 and -0.85)
summary( fmGLM$cloglog)
fmGLM$logit <- glm( PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset=log(transectArea), data=datPA, family=binomial(link="logit"))
#estimates are more dissimilar, but that is probably because there is a different link.
summary( fmGLM$logit)

###########
#Now let's try the same with inla()
fmINLA <- list()
fmINLA$cloglog <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic")
#this seems to have more-or-less failed with lots of errors like:
#...
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=990
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=991
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=992
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=993
#...
#In fact, there appears to be an error for each datum, possibly for each iteration of the optimisation
#Perhaps not surprisingly, the estimates are... not similar.  Probably stuck at starting values?
summary( fmINLA$cloglog)

#will logit be any different?
fmINLA$logit <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                       family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="logit"), inla.mode="classic")
#no warning/error messages
#and the estimates appear to be very similar to those from the logit GLM.
summary( fmINLA$logit)

#########
#FWIW, add strong priors to effects may 'help' with the possible quasi-separation.
fmINLA$cloglog_prior1 <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean=0, prec=1/0.1))
#same errors and similar summary

#what about when the intercept prior is shifted to be negative -- may affect starting values?
fmINLA$cloglog_prior2 <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, prec.intercept=1))

##########
#FWIW, reducing scale of offset or removing completely doesn't seem to solve the problem either
#is it a problem with the size of the offset?
#no, but there are fewer NAN/INF warnings
fmINLA$smallerOffset <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea/1000000), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, prec.intercept=1))

fmINLA$noOffset <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = 0, data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, prec.intercept=1))

> > >

> > >
> > > #data available from

> > >
> > > datPA <- readRDS( "~/play/cloglogIssues/datPA.RDS")
> > >
> > > ############

> > > #Fit the model that simulated the data. Note offset and pretty

> > > control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
> > >  control.fixed=list(mean=0, prec=1/0.1))
> > > #same errors and similar summary
> > >
> > > #what about when the intercept prior is shifted to be negative --
> > > may
> > > affect starting values?

> > > control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",

> > >                  family = "binomial",
> > > control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",

parts:
Hi,

The test version has nearly completely fixed our problem -- thanks Håvard!  I do sometime still get the error, but I suspect that these could possibly be the same sort of extreme edge effects that causes numerical issues in all link funcitons.

I don't get the error for GLIB_2.29.  I'm running on a machine that I do not administrate though, so I don't have much more information.

I do get a bunch of output though ("OMP: Info #268: OMP_NESTED variable deprecated, please use OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS instead.").  This is repeated many times from my code -- once for the INLA model estimation and then repeatedly from inla.posterior.summary.  sink() and invisible() don't seem to touch it either.

Overall though, I'm content that things are working.

Scott

Hi, 

We've run into some issues with using a cloglog model for
binary 
data 
(reproducibile in a simple glm).   In particular, we're
getting a 
message of (e.g.) "GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF
values in 
logl for idx=789" for each observation (and seemingly for 
each/many 
iterations).  The problem is not produced when using a logit
link 
or 
when using the glm() function from base R. 

The model does contain an offset, which has large values,
but 
reducing/removing this doesn't seem to have any effect. 

I don't know how to fix this problem.  I reckon (uneducated 
guesses 
really) that 

1) It is a user error 
2) There is numerical overflow issues (so that predictions
are 
very 
slightly above (below) 1 (0)) 
3) The starting values are very far from the max 
4) some combination of 3 and 4. 

I have put code and simulated data in a dropbox folder.  Let
me 
know 
if you can't access it. 
https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/00e4dko767yn42gnv1zoz/cloglogIssue1.R?rlkey=lr5gbo3488b7kyqt6z662yw2z&dl=0
 




.  Script is pasted below (but data still on dropbox). 

Any help is appreciated. Thanks, 

Scott 


library( INLA) 

#data available from 
https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/tihsg9da53c6ar5z50vet/datPA.RDS?rlkey=im06zt0jnlssz1izpexsne346&dl=0
 





datPA <- readRDS( "~/play/cloglogIssues/datPA.RDS") 

############ 
#Fit some models using glm() 
fmGLM <- list() 
#Fit the model that simulated the data. Note offset and
pretty 
small 
intercept (negative on link scale) 
#The fit 'works', up to some possible quasi-separation
issues 
(haven't 
investigated) 
fmGLM$cloglog <- glm( PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, 
offset=log(transectArea), data=datPA, 
family=binomial(link="cloglog")) 
#estimates are quite similar to those used to simulate (1.25
and - 
0.85) 
summary( fmGLM$cloglog) 
fmGLM$logit <- glm( PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, 
offset=log(transectArea), data=datPA, 
family=binomial(link="logit")) 
#estimates are more dissimilar, but that is probably because
there 
is 
a different link. 
summary( fmGLM$logit) 

########### 
#Now let's try the same with inla() 
fmINLA <- list() 
fmINLA$cloglog <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset =
log( 
datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1, 
                 family = "binomial", 
control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic") 
#this seems to have more-or-less failed with lots of errors
like: 
#... 
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for
idx=990 
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for
idx=991 
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for
idx=992 
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for
idx=993 
#... 
#In fact, there appears to be an error for each datum,
possibly 
for 
each iteration of the optimisation 
#Perhaps not surprisingly, the estimates are... not similar.
 Probably 
stuck at starting values? 
summary( fmINLA$cloglog) 

#will logit be any different? 
fmINLA$logit <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset =
log( 
datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1, 
                       family = "binomial", 
control.family=list(link="logit"), inla.mode="classic") 
#no warning/error messages 
#and the estimates appear to be very similar to those from
the 
logit 
GLM. 
summary( fmINLA$logit) 

######### 
#FWIW, add strong priors to effects may 'help' with the
possible 
quasi-separation. 
fmINLA$cloglog_prior1 <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4,
offset = 
log( 
datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1, 
                 family = "binomial", 
control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic", 
 control.fixed=list(mean=0, prec=1/0.1)) 
#same errors and similar summary 

#what about when the intercept prior is shifted to be
negative -- 
may 
affect starting values? 
fmINLA$cloglog_prior2 <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4,
offset = 
log( 
datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1, 
                 family = "binomial", 
control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic", 
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, 
prec.intercept=1)) 

########## 
#FWIW, reducing scale of offset or removing completely
doesn't 
seem to 
solve the problem either 
#is it a problem with the size of the offset? 
#no, but there are fewer NAN/INF warnings 
fmINLA$smallerOffset <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4,
offset = 
log( 
datPA$transectArea/1000000), data=datPA, Ntrials=1, 
                 family = "binomial", 
control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic", 
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, 
prec.intercept=1)) 

fmINLA$noOffset <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset =
0, 
data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
